summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on home hemodialysis, a mechanical aortic valve on anticoagulation, chronic diastolic heart failure, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for dark, tarry stools and weakness. She was found to have acute blood loss anemia with a hemoglobin of 8.0 g/dL and received three units of packed red blood cells. Evaluation with esophagogastroduodenoscopy, colonoscopy, and capsule endoscopy did not identify an active bleeding source, though angioectasia and polyps were noted. Warfarin was held and a heparin drip initiated, later transitioned back to warfarin. Her INR remained subtherapeutic at 2.2 at discharge, but she elected to leave with close outpatient follow-up. Hypertension was managed with increased labetalol, and dialysis was continued inpatient. She was discharged home with services, instructions to monitor for recurrent bleeding, check INR at dialysis, and follow up with vascular surgery and gastroenterology.
problems: Heart valve replaced by other means
Angiodysplasia of intestine (without mention of hemorrhage)
Diverticulosis of colon (without mention of hemorrhage)
